messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing a sudden spike in 502/523s from inference frontends in us-east-1 around 07:12 UTC. Flow logs show a ton of outbound connections getting RST and NAT egress port util at ~99%.

sre-bot: Alert: nat-egress-port-utilization > 95% (us-east-1a,us-east-1b)

raj: Is the traffic coming from model pulls or from real-time user requests?

oliver: Quick glance: sidecar logs show a burst of short-lived connections to huggingface.co and public S3 URLs right before the errors. Lots of sockets in TIME_WAIT on the egress path.

alice: Adding metrics — conntrack table usage on our NAT instances (we still run a small fleet in the fallback AZ) peaked and nf_conntrack dropped entries. NAT Gateway metrics show ephemeral port allocation hitting the limit per ENI. Looks like combination of very high concurrent outbound sockets + hairpinning to public endpoints.

maria: Hairpinning? What’s the path that forces NAT here — are we resolving to public IPs for internal services or using public model URLs?

oliver: We discovered some services using the public huggingface URLs instead of our internal mirror. So pods in private subnets fetch models via public IP -> goes through NAT -> back through internet -> and some traffic ends up routed back to our ALB / public target — that adds extra egress load and ports.

raj: Immediate mitigation suggestions: throttle the model pull workers + enable client-side backoff. Also, flip model fetches to use VPC endpoints / internal mirror.

alice: For NAT instances we can bump conntrack max and tune TIME_WAIT recycling, e.g.:
```
# on NAT instance only (if using NAT instances)
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```
But note NAT Gateway (managed) won’t accept these; its portspace per ENI is finite.

infra-eng: Short-term operational play: 1) scale up additional NAT Gateways across more AZs (split subnet routes to spread load), 2) add an egress proxy (Envoy) with keepalive connection pooling to huggingface/S3, 3) throttle model pull concurrency. I’ll start a canary for the egress proxy on one nodepool.

maria: If NAT Gateway is elastic, why are we still hitting limits? I thought it scales.

oliver: NAT GW is managed and elastic, but practical limits exist due to ephemeral port allocation on each ENI and per-AZ behavior. If a large fraction of connections come from many pods simultaneously and they resolve to public IPs, you can exhaust portspace before the system balances across ENIs. Also hairpinning doubles the egress load.

raj: Another fast workaround: route model fetches through a private ALB/internal mirror (no egress), or create S3 VPC Gateway/Interface endpoints and host model artifacts in a private bucket or CloudFront with origin access. That eliminates NAT completely for those flows.

alice: Operational tasks I’m adding to the runbook: instrument per-pod outbound socket counts, add alert when single-subnet port util > 80%, and add an automated throttling feature for background fetchers. Runbook note: if you use NAT instances, increase nf_conntrack and monitor conntrack drops; if NAT GW, prefer moving traffic to VPC endpoints.

infra-eng: Quick canary status: deploying envoy egress proxy with HTTP/2 to huggingface mirror. Config uses connection multiplexing and keepalive: fewer sockets, much lower TIME_WAIT.

maria: I’ll patch the orchestrator to limit max concurrent pulls per nodepool (50 -> 8) and add staggered startup. Pushing the change now.

raj: Long term: host an internal model cache, use signed VPC-only URLs, and ensure service DNS resolves to internal IPs when called from inside the VPC (split-horizon). Also consider using persistent HTTP/2 or gRPC streams for artifact transfer to cut socket churn.

oliver: For immediate recovery if we keep seeing errors: move affected subnets to alternate NAT (other AZ) to redistribute ephemeral ports, or bring up a NAT instance with tuned conntrack as emergency stopgap.

maria: Thanks — tagging folks to follow up: @alice @raj @infra-eng. Meeting in 15 to confirm mitigations and rollback plan.

deploy-bot: Can confirm deployment of egress-proxy-canary to nodepool/model-fetchers-1 started at 07:36 UTC.
